Guy de Maupassant, Pierre and Jean, translated by Clara Bell.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/guy-de-maupassant/pierre-and-jean/clara-bell

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Guy de Maupassant, the author, annotator and writer of the introduction or preface, died 1893 (Wikidata Q9327, P570 1893-07-06).
- Clara Bell, the translator, died 1927 (Wikidata Q1091668, P570 1927-01-16).

First publication of the text used: 1902, the English translation by Clara Bell. The French original was published in 1888. The country of first publication of the translation is not stated in the facts. (SE colophon: 'Pierre and Jean was published in 1888 by Guy de Maupassant. It was translated from French in 1902 by Clara Bell.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1902 and the original in 1888, both before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Two layers, checked separately. Original: French work by Guy de Maupassant (died 1893), first published 1888. The author died before 1926, so the original is public domain in every country. Translation (English): the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life + 70 years or less. The translator Clara Bell (died 1927) left the public domain in each of them on 1 January 1998, so the translation is public domain in each. The country of first publication therefore makes no difference.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
